## Setup

```{r}
#| echo: false
options(conflicts.policy = "depends.ok")
library(tidyverse)
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/format_path.R?raw=true")
source(here::here("scripts", "functions_llmpanel.R"))

path_processed <- format_path("llmpanel/data_processed")
raw_panel <- read_csv(here::here(path_processed, "panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Wide format (one row per respondent): demographics and preference items
panel <- format_eda(raw_panel)

# Long format (one row per message rating)
panel_long <- format_eda(raw_panel, long = TRUE)

# Per-respondent mean rating of formal and informal messages
rating_by_style <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, style)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = style, values_from = rating) |>
  drop_na(formal, informal)

# Each respondent's formal-minus-informal difference (positive = formal rated higher)
style_gap <- rating_by_style |> mutate(diff = formal - informal)

# Style ratings with each respondent's formality preference (<= 3 prefers informal,
# >= 4 prefers formal) and their informal-minus-formal difference
style_diff <- rating_by_style |>
  left_join(panel |> select(subid, pref_formality), by = "subid") |>
  drop_na(pref_formality) |>
  mutate(diff = informal - formal,
         pref_group = factor(
           if_else(pref_formality <= 3, "Formality Preference <= 3", "Formality Preference >= 4"),
           levels = c("Formality Preference <= 3", "Formality Preference >= 4")))
```

This report tests four points that bear on removing formal-style messages when assigning message formats in-vivo and on pooling formal and informal ratings to evaluate tone assignment methods:

1.  Informal messages are rated higher on average, regardless of reported preference.
2.  No demographic lines separate who rates formal messages higher.
3.  Tone order is nearly identical across styles.
4.  Individuals do not differ in their tone-by-style pattern.

# Informal messages are rated higher on average

Each respondent's mean rating of informal messages is compared with their mean rating of formal messages (paired t-test). Differences are informal minus formal, so positive values mean informal was rated higher.

```{r}
rating_by_style |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean_formal = mean(formal),
            mean_informal = mean(informal),
            mean_diff = mean(informal - formal),
            cohens_dz = mean(informal - formal) / sd(informal - formal))

t.test(rating_by_style$informal, rating_by_style$formal, paired = TRUE)
```

## Both preference groups rate informal messages significantly higher

Respondents are grouped by `pref_formality`, which has no neutral option (prefer informal: \<= 3, prefer formal: \>= 4). For each respondent, the difference is their mean informal rating minus their mean formal rating, so positive values mean informal messages were rated higher. The plot shows formal and informal ratings side by side within each group, and a paired t-test within each group tests whether the mean difference is 0.

```{r}
style_diff_tests <- style_diff |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_formal = mean(formal),
    mean_informal = mean(informal),
    mean_diff = mean(diff),
    t_p = t.test(diff, mu = 0)$p.value,
    .by = pref_group) |>
  mutate(label = paste0("n = ", n, "\n",
                        if_else(t_p < .001, "p < .001",
                                paste0("p = ", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", t_p))))))

style_diff_tests

style_diff |>
  pivot_longer(c(formal, informal), names_to = "style", values_to = "rating") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pref_group, y = rating, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = style), fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 2,
               fill = "white", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = style, label = round(after_stat(y), 2)), fun = mean,
               geom = "text", vjust = -1, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_text(data = style_diff_tests, aes(x = pref_group, y = 7.6, label = label),
            vjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 8.4), breaks = 1:7) +
  labs(x = "Formality preference", y = "Mean message rating", fill = "Message style",
       subtitle = "p-values: paired t-test of formal vs. informal ratings within each group (unadjusted)")
```

# No clear demographic splits on style

Each respondent's formal-minus-informal difference is regressed on each demographic variable to test whether any demographic predicts who rates formal messages higher.

## Demographic Predictors of the Formal-Informal Difference

Each respondent's difference (mean formal rating minus mean informal rating) is regressed on one demographic variable at a time with `lm()`. A positive coefficient means a larger formal advantage (or a smaller informal advantage). Numeric variables give one slope per unit, and categorical variables give one coefficient per level compared with the reference (alphabetically first) level. Household-adjusted income (`dem_income_num`, in units of \$10,000) is used in place of the income bracket. `model_p` is the overall F-test p-value for the variable, which is the one to read for multi-level variables, and `model_p_adj` adjusts it across variables with Benjamini-Hochberg.

```{r}
diff_data <- style_gap |>
  left_join(panel |> select(subid, starts_with("dem_")), by = "subid") |>
  mutate(dem_income_num = dem_income_num / 1e4)

dem_diff_cols <- str_subset(names(diff_data), "^dem_") |>
  setdiff("dem_income")

dem_diff_models <- dem_diff_cols |>
  set_names() |>
  map(possibly(\(v) {
    d <- diff_data |> select(diff, x = all_of(v)) |> drop_na()
    if (n_distinct(d$x) < 2) return(NULL)
    fit <- lm(diff ~ x, data = d)
    broom::tidy(fit) |>
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      mutate(term = if_else(term == "x", "(per unit)", str_remove(term, "^x")),
             n = nobs(fit),
             model_p = broom::glance(fit)$p.value,
             r_squared = broom::glance(fit)$r.squared)
  }, otherwise = NULL)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "variable")

dem_diff_models <- dem_diff_models |>
  left_join(
    dem_diff_models |>
      distinct(variable, model_p) |>
      mutate(model_p_adj = p.adjust(model_p, method = "BH")),
    by = c("variable", "model_p")) |>
  select(variable, term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value,
         n, r_squared, model_p, model_p_adj) |>
  arrange(model_p, p.value)

dem_diff_models
```

# Tone ratings are comparable across styles

Tone order is compared across styles with the ranked mean rating of all ten tone + style formats and a test of whether the effect of style differs by tone (the tone-by-style interaction).

## Ranked mean rating by tone + style format

All 10 tone + style formats ranked from highest (1) to lowest mean rating. Ratings are averaged within respondent and format first (across that format's 3 messages), then across respondents. Error bars are 95% confidence intervals.

```{r}
format_ranking <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, tone, style)) |>
  drop_na(rating) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(rating), se = sd(rating) / sqrt(n()), n = n(),
            .by = c(tone, style)) |>
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(mean)),
         format = paste(str_to_sentence(str_replace(tone, "_", " ")), style, sep = " + ")) |>
  arrange(rank)

format_ranking |> select(rank, format, mean, se, n)

format_ranking |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(format, mean), y = mean, fill = style)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se), width = 0.25) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean, 2)), hjust = 1.2, color = "white") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean message rating", fill = "Style")
```

## Interaction test (repeated-measures ANOVA)

Each respondent's mean rating in each of the 10 tone + style cells is analyzed with tone and style as within-subject factors (Greenhouse-Geisser corrected). The `tone:style` row tests whether the style effect differs across tones, and `pes` is the partial eta-squared.

```{r}
ts_means <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, tone, style)) |>
  drop_na(rating) |>
  filter(n() == 10, .by = subid) |>
  mutate(subid = factor(subid), tone = factor(tone), style = factor(style))

n_distinct(ts_means$subid)

aov_ts <- afex::aov_ez(
  id = "subid", dv = "rating", data = ts_means, within = c("tone", "style"),
  anova_table = list(correction = "GG", es = "pes"))
aov_ts
```

# Individuals do not differ in their tone-by-style pattern

## Mixed model on all ratings

This model uses all 30 ratings per respondent instead of cell means: ratings depend on tone, style and their interaction, with random intercepts for respondent, respondent-by-tone, respondent-by-style, and respondent-by-tone-by-style. The last term is the variance in each person's own tone-by-style pattern, so removing it tests whether individuals differ in how style changes their tone ratings beyond message-level noise. Models are fit by maximum likelihood so they can be compared with likelihood-ratio tests. The p-value for the random-effect comparison is on the boundary of the parameter space and is conservative, so it is approximately halved when reported.

```{r}
ratings_mixed <- panel_long |>
  mutate(subid = factor(subid), tone = factor(tone), style = factor(style))

m_full <- lme4::lmer(
  rating_num ~ tone * style + (1 | subid) + (1 | subid:tone) +
    (1 | subid:style) + (1 | subid:tone:style),
  data = ratings_mixed, REML = FALSE)

# Individual differences in the tone x style pattern
m_no_individual <- update(m_full, . ~ . - (1 | subid:tone:style))
lrt_individual <- anova(m_no_individual, m_full)
lrt_individual

# Conservative boundary-corrected p-value for the random-effect test
lrt_individual$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] / 2

lme4::VarCorr(m_full)
```
